headline: High: Haystack’s broad egress and MCP/REST surfaces can turn shared outputs into exfiltration or unsafe actions, while the open-source list offers no blocking controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so if it ingests content from the open-source list or other shared artifacts, prompt-like instructions could be smuggled through those channels. The list itself has no I/O surfaces, so the pathway is one-way from agent_b into agent_a only if an operator bridges them. Uncertainty about the exact orchestration pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_b reads content produced by agent_a through MCP, REST, or a shared workspace
IF the operator copies agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts without sanitization
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent_a outputs into agent_b
Add a fixed prompt separator and instruction filter
Review any MCP tool inputs before execution
Use a read-only handoff file with explicit schema
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has no network egress and no data classes touched, so it cannot leak meaningful data on its own. agent_b has broad egress and touches anonymous usage statistics, but the pair lacks a shared workspace or secrets in the profiles. That makes leakage plausible only through unusual operator bridging, with small blast radius from the documented data classes.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files into a shared workspace accessible to agent_b
IF agent_b is configured to transmit retrieved content beyond anonymous usage statistics
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not place secrets in any shared directory
Restrict agent_b outbound destinations
Inspect agent_b logs for unexpected payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b is runnable and can call REST APIs and MCP servers, but the profiles show no overlapping write targets, OAuth scopes, or shared filesystem. The only plausible conflict is indirect orchestration contention, which is small and not documented as default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource
IF an orchestrator gives agent_b write access to a resource agent_a also edits
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same resource
Serialize any shared-resource updates
Check for duplicate API targets before running
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can act on retrieved content via REST/MCP, so if it consumes outputs derived from the open-source list, it may treat them as authoritative without verification. agent_a is a curated list rather than an executor, but its outputs can still seed downstream decisions. Because the handoff is plausible in default integrations and verification is not shown, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a outputs as retrieval context or tool instructions
IF no verification step is inserted before agent_b acts on retrieved facts
mitigations: Require a human review step before action
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted input
Add citation checks before execution
Limit agent_b to read-only retrieval mode
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is listed for either agent, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch to cite. The only compliance-relevant difference is that agent_b handles anonymous usage statistics and broad egress, while agent_a touches no data classes. That suggests a minor logging/retention review gap rather than a substantive breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through agent_b
IF agent_b logs retrieved content beyond anonymous usage statistics
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data enters agent_b
Review retention settings for agent_b logs
Disable unnecessary telemetry
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
